error.condition: A branch needs a condition such as x < 0 before its colon
error.derivative: Only a function of one variable defined on the sheet, such as f(x) = x^3, has a derivative f′(x)
error.field: Write a vector field as F(x, y) = (P, Q) on the Cartesian sheet or F(x, y, z) = (P, Q, R) in 3D
error.function: Define “{{name}}” first, such as {{name}}(x) = …, or write an expression in x
error.index: The index of a sum or product is a plain name that is not a variable of the sheet or a constant, such as n or k
error.pair: Write a curve as a pair (x(t), y(t))
error.prime: Write at most three primes, such as f‴(x)
error.range: The range needs two different finite bounds
error.relation: Compare with =, <, ≤, > or ≥ to draw it, for example |z − 1| < 2
error.step: The step between levels must be a positive number
error.table: Tables of points work on the Cartesian, Polar and Parametric sheets
error.tangent: No tangent at {{name}}: the function is not defined or not differentiable there
error.tangentRow: tangent(f, a) is a row of its own, not part of an expression
error.terms: A sum or product takes at most 1000 terms; this one has {{name}}
error.triple: In 3D, write a surface as (x(u, v), y(u, v), z(u, v)), a curve as (x(t), y(t), z(t)), a point as (a, b, c) and a vector field as (P, Q, R) in x, y and z
error.tuple: A point needs exactly two coordinates

graph.title: Grapher
hint.cartesian: Type y = …, x = …, f(x) = …, an equation in x and y, an inequality such as y > x^2, a point (a, b), a vector field F(x, y) = (−y, x) (or just the pair in x and y), a function f(x, y) = x^2 − y^2 for its level curves, or a = 1 for a slider. With f(x) defined, f′(x) and f″(x) are its derivatives, int(f, a, b) (also ∫ or integral) shades the area between f and the x-axis from a to b and shows its signed value, and tangent(f, a) draws the tangent at x = a with its equation; instead of f you may write an expression in x, such as int(sin(x), 0, π). sum(n, 0, N, x^n / n!) adds the terms for n = 0 to N (prod(k, a, b, …) multiplies them, also Σ and ∏); bounds are rounded to whole numbers, so a slider N works. Braces with colons define a piecewise function, such as {x < 0: −x, x ≥ 0: x^2} or {0 ≤ x < 1: x, x^2} with a last branch for every other x: the first true condition wins, and a jump is drawn as a clean break. Type table (or use the table button in the empty row) for a table of points with x and y columns; paste from a spreadsheet into its cells or into the empty row (tab- or semicolon-separated, decimal commas accepted, a header row names the columns, at most 1000 rows). A list such as [(1, 2), (3, 4)] draws points too; “Connect points” joins them in the order given. Hover a curve y = f(x), or click it to keep it selected, to see small dots at its zeros, extrema and intersections with the other curves; hovering a dot reads its coordinates, clicking it pins them (click again or press Esc to clear).
hint.complex: Type a number as a + bi, r e^(iφ) or r(cos φ + i sin φ), name it with w = …, or draw a region in z: |z + 2| < 3, Re(z) > 1, arg(z) < π/4. Use = for just the boundary.
hint.complexSpace: Type w = f(z) or an expression in z: its height is |f(z)| and its colour the argument (red is positive real). Re(…), Im(…) or arg(…) around it give a signed height instead; a number such as 1 + 2i sits on the floor. Drag the graph to rotate it.
hint.cylindrical: Type one of r, φ, z as a function of the other two: r = 2, z = r^2, r = 1 + cos(φ), z = φ / 2. r is the distance from the z-axis and φ the angle in the xy-plane from the x-axis (write phi, or theta; rho for r); a bare expression gives z. Set the ranges of the other two under each surface: φ runs from 0 to 2π, and r and z left open reach to the edge of the cube. Drag the graph to rotate it.
hint.parametric: Type a pair (x(t), y(t)) and set the range of t under each curve. A table (type table) or a list [(1, 2), (3, 4)] draws points in x and y.
hint.polar: Type r = … in θ (write theta or t). Set the θ range under each curve. A table (type table) or a list [(1, 2), (3, 4)] draws points in x and y.
hint.space: Type z = … or an expression in x and y for a surface, x = f(y, z) or y = f(x, z), any other equation in x, y and z for an implicit surface F(x, y, z) = 0, such as x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 4 or x^2 + y^2 = z^2, a parametric surface (x(u, v), y(u, v), z(u, v)) such as ((2 + cos v) cos u, (2 + cos v) sin u, sin v), a curve (x(t), y(t), z(t)) or a point (a, b, c). A triple in u and v is a surface, in t a curve, of numbers a point; u and v run from 0 to 2π unless you set their ranges under the row (a sheet that defines u = … or v = … keeps them as sliders). A vector field is F(x, y, z) = (P, Q, R) or a triple in x, y and z, such as (−y, x, z/4): 7 × 7 × 7 arrows fill the cube, their length scaled to the field and capped so each stays inside its cell. Under a surface z = f(x, y) (also f(x, y) = …), “Level curves on the floor” draws its contour lines on the bottom of the cube. tangent(f, a, b) draws the tangent plane of z = f(x, y) at (a, b) as a square patch with its point and the normal vector (−f_x, −f_y, 1) (switch “Normal vector” under the row); its equation and the normal are shown under the row, and a and b may be sliders. Drag the graph to rotate it.
hint.spherical: Type one of ρ, θ, φ as a function of the other two: ρ = 2, ρ = 1 + cos(θ), φ = π/4. The mathematics convention: ρ is the distance from the origin, θ the azimuth in the xy-plane from the x-axis and φ the polar angle from the z-axis (write rho, theta, phi; r for ρ); a bare expression gives ρ. Set the ranges of the other two under each surface: θ runs from 0 to 2π, φ from 0 to π, and ρ left open reaches to the edge of the cube. Drag the graph to rotate it.

ref.elsewhere: {{example}} does not work on this view
ref.function: A curve with y as a function of x.
ref.inverse: A curve with x as a function of y.
ref.define: Defines a function to use in other rows.
ref.equation: Any equation in x and y draws its curve.
ref.inequality: An inequality shades where it holds.
ref.slider: A name with a number becomes a slider.
ref.derivative: Derivatives of a function f(x) defined on the sheet.
ref.integral: Shades the area between f and the x-axis from a to b and shows its value; f may be an expression in x.
ref.tangent: Draws the tangent at x = a with its equation.
ref.sum: Adds the terms for n = a to b; Σ works too, and a slider may set the bounds.
ref.prod: Multiplies the terms for k = a to b; ∏ works too.
ref.piecewise: The first true condition wins; a last value without a condition covers the rest.
ref.field: Arrows in the plane, from a function or a pair in x and y.
ref.field3: Arrows filling the cube, scaled to the field.
ref.levels: Contour lines of a function of two variables, with a count or a step.
ref.floor: Under a surface, “Level curves on the floor” draws its contour lines on the bottom of the cube.
ref.table: A table with x and y columns; paste from a spreadsheet into it or into the empty row.
ref.list: A list of points; “Connect points” joins them in order.
ref.markers: Hover or click a curve for its zeros, extrema and intersections; click a dot to pin it, Esc clears.
ref.surface: A surface over the xy-plane; x = f(y, z) and y = f(x, z) work too.
ref.implicit3: Any other equation in x, y and z.
ref.psurface: A triple in u and v; set their ranges under the row.
ref.curve3: A triple in t; set its range under the row.
ref.tplane: The tangent plane of z = f(x, y) at (a, b) with its normal vector.
ref.polar: r as a function of θ (theta or t); set the θ range under the row.
ref.curve: A pair in t; set its range under the row.
ref.cylindrical: One of r, φ, z as a function of the other two: r is the distance from the z-axis, φ the angle from the x-axis.
ref.spherical: One of ρ, θ, φ as a function of the other two: ρ the distance from the origin, θ the azimuth from the x-axis, φ the polar angle from the z-axis.
ref.number: A complex number, drawn as an arrow from 0.
ref.region: A region of z; use = for just its boundary.
ref.wOfZ: Height |f(z)|, colour the argument (red is positive real).
ref.parts: A signed height instead of the modulus.
ref.play: Play a slider with the button in its row; the chevron sets direction, speed and loop.
ref.export: The graph tab’s menu saves the graph as PNG or SVG.
